standard_prerequisites.name: Chow's lemma and the behaviour of intersection numbers under a birational proper pullback
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Cohomology of Schemes, labels coherent-lemma-chow-Noetherian (proof line 8221) and coherent-remark-chow-Noetherian (proof line 8222); Varieties, label varieties-lemma-intersection-number-and-pullback (proof line 8227)
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the H-projective birational model Y of X over which the computation may be done and shows the intersection number is unchanged by that pullback.

standard_prerequisites.name: Compatibility of capping with a first Chern class with pushforward, additivity of both sides and the effective Cartier divisor case
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter chow.tex, labels lemma-pushforward-cap-c1 (proof line 8233), lemma-c1-cap-additive (proof line 8244) and lemma-geometric-cap (proof line 8254); Divisors, label divisors-lemma-quasi-projective-Noetherian-pic-effective-Cartier (proof line 8241); Varieties, labels varieties-lemma-intersection-number-additive (proof line 8243) and varieties-lemma-numerical-intersection-effective-Cartier-divisor (proof line 8248)
standard_prerequisites.use: Moves the equality across the birational model, reduces an invertible sheaf to a difference of two effective Cartier divisors by additivity of both sides, and rewrites both sides in the divisor case so that the induction hypothesis applies.

core_obligations: Reduce to a proper variety of dimension d: write [Z]_d as the sum over the components with multiplicities and use the analogous decomposition of the intersection number to reduce to Z = X, then apply Chow's lemma to replace X by an H-projective birational model Y and observe both sides are unchanged under that pullback (proof lines 8201-8234).

Reduce to a single effective Cartier divisor: write the first invertible sheaf as O_X(D) tensor O_X(D')^{-1} for effective Cartier divisors D and D' on the projective X, then use additivity of the intersection number and of capping with c_1 to reduce to L_1 = O_X(D) (proof lines 8236-8246).

Close the induction on d: for L_1 = O_X(D) the intersection number (L_1 ... L_d . X) equals (L_2 ... L_d . D) and the cycle c_1(L_1) cap ... cap c_1(L_d) cap [X] equals c_1(L_2) cap ... cap c_1(L_d) cap [D]_{d-1}, so the assertion for d follows from the induction hypothesis applied to the divisor D of dimension d - 1 (proof lines 8247-8259).
proof_roadmap: Split over the components and reduce to a proper variety, then to an H-projective one by Chow's lemma (proof lines 8201-8234).
Reduce the first invertible sheaf to an effective Cartier divisor by additivity (proof lines 8236-8246).
Rewrite both sides on the divisor and conclude by induction on the dimension (proof lines 8247-8259).
difficulty_reason: The lemma identifies the numerical intersection number (L_1 ... L_d . Z) of d invertible sheaves against a d-dimensional closed subscheme of a proper scheme over a field with the degree of the iterated cap product of their first Chern classes with the fundamental class, and specialises to the self-intersection of an ample sheaf (statement lines 8180-8198, tag 0BFI). The proof is a genuine three-stage reduction: over the components, then to an H-projective birational model via Chow's lemma, then to the case of a single effective Cartier divisor where the geometric case of the top Chern class converts both sides into the same expression on the divisor, allowing induction on the dimension. Each reduction is an argument in its own right, so the claim is H2.
